literal: When painting, like the eyes indeed that do not see the painting rod, I do not see the faults of my husband when I see him.
translation: Just like the eyes that cannot see the painting-rod while collyrium is being applied to them, I cannot see any of my husband's faults when he is before me.
modern: கண்களுக்கு மை தீட்டும்போது அந்த மையைத் தீட்டும் கோலைத் தன் கண்கள் காணாதது போல, என் கணவனை நான் நேரில் காணும்போது அவனுடைய தவறுகள் எதையும் நான் காண்பதில்லை.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine describes her inability to hold a grudge or remember her husband's faults once he is in her presence. She compares this to the act of applying collyrium to the eyes. When the painting-rod ('kōl') comes extremely close to the eyes to beautify them, the eyes themselves cannot see the rod. Similarly, when her beloved husband ('koṇkaṉ') is close to her, his physical presence and love completely overwhelm her, making it impossible for her to see or remember any of his flaws ('paḻi') that she had previously intended to confront him about.
